description.value:
"Everything's a door if you hold it right."

Operator is the Intrigue Calling — the trade that kept its bearers alive after the Shattering. Umbrella: thief, smuggler, spy, courier, fence, hacker, fixer. A profession is a flavor label on the Calling.

Knack — Underfoot: In crowds, markets, and streets, the Operator passes unremarked unless actively hunted; Streetwise checks never fumble (at Tier III, also Stealth).

Aptitude kit: signature aptitude Stealth rank = tier; secondary Streetwise rank = tier − 1.

Services: a standard job costs the tier fee (T1 10 / T2 30 / T3 90 / T4 270 marks), paid in Intrigue marks. Cross-pool ×1.5 friction applies as usual.

Tiers: Apprentice → Initiate → Master → Archon. Grant the matching tier features alongside this class item.

Awakens into: Shadow Courier. A Steward is a Calling that ignited into a Path — Surge is the mark of Stewardship, which is why no Calling banks or spends it.

Operator — Apprentice (Tier I).

Trade — Carry it quiet: Move a package/message across town, no questions. Standard fee 10 marks (Intrigue).

Trick — Pocketed (1/scene): Produce a mundane Tier-I item they plausibly lifted earlier.

Echoes are the past made flesh — people out of a Steward's former lives, walking beside them again. Marisol Quint is an echo of Toblerone's time with the Covert Ops Cell crew. Being remembered leaves a mark.

Forger — She still cuts your travel papers for free because the last set you forged for her kept a Sweet Release skimmer out of a Monodynamic cage.

Never Here — Apprentice (Echo Boon)

Once per scene, retroactively establish the echo was somewhere else; one witness's account of them unravels.

Echo's Mark: while their Steward can see them, the echo adds +1 on any check made in direct support of the Steward.

Officially, this person does not exist. Officially never changed.

Circuitborn. Normalized Bad Eden ancestry root.

Select one heritage separately when building the character: Exo-Knight, Parallax, Salvage, Synapse.

This root grants the shared Circuitborn core trait package (Firmware of Identity) and preserves live UUID compatibility for the four Line items.

“You are not a robot. You are a decision the world keeps making about itself. The networks are alive and they recognize you on sight.”

Firmware of Identity. You do not eat, drink, or sleep. You enter maintenance trance when you rest. You reroll the lowest die on checks against poison and disease, and you are immune to magical sleep.

Attention Resonance. 1/Soma Break, when a creature you can see is intensely focused on you, you may regain either one spent Bad Eden OP (a category you used this scene) or Integrity equal to your tier.

Informational Matrix Sense. You can feel active networks: radio, signal, ritual, rumor.

Line Memory. Choose one Circuitborn line (Exo-Knight, Parallax, Salvage, Synapse). Your line grants Tier powers as you level.

description.value:
“You are not a robot. You are a decision the world keeps making about itself.”

Firmware of Identity. You do not eat, drink, or sleep. You enter maintenance trance when you rest. You reroll the lowest die on checks against poison and disease, and you are immune to magical sleep.

Attention Resonance. 1/Soma Break, when a creature you can see is intensely focused on you (ally or enemy; GM adjudicates), you may regain either (a) one spent Bad Eden OP (a category you used this scene) or (b) Integrity equal to your tier.

Informational Matrix Sense. You can feel active networks: radio, signal, ritual, rumor. You reroll the lowest die on checks to identify surveillance, hidden speakers, encoded messages, or noospheric “attention traps.”

Glitch-Surge. When you drop to 0 Integrity, you can choose to emit a controlled burst of static (no damage, but loud and disorienting) before you fall. In Bad Eden play, this is a perfect excuse for weird consequences.

description.value:
Circuitborn Line. The ghost-in-the-protocol. The chassis that thinks faster than the network it’s plugged into, and feels the noosphere the way a swimmer feels the current.

“You don’t use the network. The network uses you, and that’s the only relationship that doesn’t collapse.”

Synapse. You are a sentient chassis built around the principle of inference. Information is your home. Other people travel through it. You live there.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Construct-Living).
  • Chassis Lean. Your chassis is built around MND (Mind)—expressed primarily through Tier powers.
  • Predictive Cache. 1/Soma Break, when an enemy you can see takes an action, you may have anticipated it: reroll the lowest die on the next reaction or attack you make against that enemy this round.

“Reality is a database. You brought admin tools.”

Yesod-Diver. You reroll the lowest die on checks to interpret metaphysical constructs (Sparks, slippage, noospheric entities). 1/Soma Break, you can ask the GM one direct question about a nearby “system,” and receive a truthful but incomplete answer.

Standard-issue field knife. Single-edge, thumb groove, hard sheath that clips to a belt or boot. The first weapon most Stewards carry and the last one they put down. Honest steel — no signature, no story, just edge.

Standard Issue. Light enough for off-hand work; close enough for the kind of conversation knives are for.

⚙️ Mechanical Effects

Light, finesse-friendly. No signature ability.

  • Damage: 1d6 Kinetic damage to Integrity (blade)
  • Faculty: Violence
  • Attack: Melee (Violence)
  • Reach: Melee
  • Duration: Scene
  • Tier: T1

Leather-wrapped lead-shot bludgeon, palm-sized. Lives in a pocket or a sleeve. Designed to put someone out without breaking anything that won't heal in a week.

Standard Issue (Subdual). Damage is subdual-flavored — narratively kinetic but easy to declare nonlethal. Useful for Couriers, intriguers, and anyone whose plan ended with "and then we walk away."

Layered travel cloth — patchwork canvas over a quilted underlayer, road-stained at the cuffs. Cut for moving. Sold on every frontier table from Allesh Gilliam to the edge of the Lyrenn line. The first armor most Stewards ever buy, and the first they outgrow.

Standard Issue. Worn in the field, not the throne room. Easy to repair, easy to replace, easy to forget you have it on.

⚙️ Mechanical Effects

  • Armor: Light
  • Defense: Guard +1, Evasion +1
  • Requires: Weave (trained)
  • Tier: I
  • Cost: 75 Nonlethal marks
